oewn-00509102-n.learner: a game in which players buy chances, or are given them, and the prizes go to whoever is picked by chance.
examples: She won a new bicycle in the drawing at the school fair.

oewn-00392901-n.learner: the act of taking or draining something, such as electricity or a liquid, from the place it comes from.
examples: The drawing of water from the well took most of the morning.

oewn-00116487-n.learner: the act of moving a load by pulling it.
examples: Horses were once used for the drawing of carts and ploughs.

oewn-00992424-v.learner: to go to someone and speak to them, usually to offer a plan or an idea.
examples: Several companies approached her with offers of work.

oewn-02709812-v.learner: to come near to something or almost be it, to be like it, or to come closer to it in quality or character.
examples: Her skill on the piano approaches that of a professional.

oewn-00604200-v.learner: to be trained or taught so that you are ready for a certain role, job, or profession.
examples: She spent three years preparing for the law.

oewn-02392176-v.learner: to teach someone so that they will be ready for a role or job later on.
examples: The old manager prepared his assistant to take over the business.

oewn-00604693-v.learner: to make someone into something by training and teaching them.
examples: The college has prepared many fine nurses.

oewn-01654986-v.learner: to arrange something by careful planning and by people working together.
examples: The committee prepared a campaign to save the old library.

oewn-02184359-v.learner: in music, to lead into a harsh-sounding chord more gently by first playing its clashing note as a pleasant-sounding part of the chord before it.
examples: The composer prepares the discord by holding the note over from the chord before.

oewn-05797094-n.learner: something that has been settled or decided; what comes out of making a decision.
examples: The two sides finally reached a resolution of their differences.

oewn-11526370-n.learner: in computing, how many tiny dots fit into each square inch of a screen; the more there are, the better the picture.
examples: This screen has a much higher resolution than my old one.

oewn-00154629-n.learner: the act of finding an answer to a problem.
examples: The resolution of the problem took the team several weeks.

oewn-06756201-n.learner: a statement that solves a problem, or that explains how the problem can be solved.
examples: The resolution to the puzzle was printed on the back page.

oewn-11526187-n.learner: how well a microscope or telescope can measure the small angle between two images that are very close together.
examples: The new telescope has a far better resolution than the old one.

oewn-05790881-n.learner: the act of breaking something down into clear, separate parts.
examples: A prism allows the resolution of white light into its colours.

oewn-07041708-n.learner: in music, a harsh-sounding chord being followed by a pleasant-sounding one.
examples: The piece ends with a slow resolution onto a quiet major chord.

oewn-07434817-n.learner: the going down of swelling or other signs that part of the body is inflamed, especially in a lung.
examples: The X-ray showed complete resolution of the infection in her lung.

oewn-08195465-n.learner: the group of people who make up the government of an independent country.
examples: The state has raised the tax on fuel again.

oewn-14011983-n.learner: a condition of feeling very low and unhappy, or of being very upset and nervous.
examples: She was in such a state that she could hardly speak.

oewn-08562388-n.learner: the land that a nation covers.
examples: The small state of Luxembourg can be crossed by car in an hour.

oewn-14503199-n.learner: in chemistry, one of the three usual forms of matter: a solid, with a fixed shape and size; a liquid, with a fixed size that takes the shape of its container; or a gas, which fills its container.
examples: Water in its solid state is called ice.

oewn-01522244-s.learner: having to do with ordinary citizens rather than with the army and other armed forces.
examples: After the war, the civil authorities took over from the army.

oewn-00413432-s.learner: having, or living in, an ordered and settled society.
examples: After months in the wilderness, the explorers were glad to be among civil peoples again.

connotation.why: ranks some peoples as ordered and others by implication as wild

oewn-00645956-a.learner: of units of time: accepted by law for use in the ordinary business of life.
examples: A civil day begins at midnight.

oewn-09358146-n.learner: the top layer of earth that plants can grow in, especially when talking about how good it is or what it is used for.
examples: The ground here is too stony for growing wheat.

oewn-13813124-n.learner: a link or position that something else is built on or rests on.
examples: The two leaders found common ground in their fear of war.

oewn-08597662-n.learner: a position that people fight to win or to keep, in a battle or in something like a battle.
examples: The army slowly gained ground against the enemy.
In the argument, neither side would give ground.

oewn-05942570-n.learner: the part of a scene or picture that lies behind the things at the front.
examples: The white flowers stand out clearly against the dark ground of the picture.

oewn-03467679-n.learner: a link joining an electrical device to something large that carries electricity, such as the earth, which is treated as having zero voltage.
examples: Connect the green wire to the ground before you switch on the power.

oewn-05939360-n.learner: the fairly even area that you see behind the shape you are paying attention to.
examples: In the drawing, the two faces are the figure and the white space between them is the ground.

oewn-03467526-n.learner: in art, the surface, such as a wall or a canvas, that has been made ready to take the paint of a painting.
examples: The painter spread fresh plaster on the wall to make a ground for the picture.

oewn-03365691-n.learner: the first coat of paint, or of size (a thin glue), put on a surface before the other coats.
examples: She brushed on a white ground before the first real coat of paint.

oewn-00231983-v.learner: to get bigger in a natural way.
examples: The tree has grown two metres since we planted it.

oewn-01743695-v.learner: to raise plants or crops, often using farming methods to make them better.
examples: My grandfather grows tomatoes and beans in his garden.

oewn-00094214-v.learner: to come to have a physical feature, or to go through a change in one.
examples: He grew a beard over the winter.

oewn-02630344-v.learner: to come into being, or to take on a form or shape.
examples: Their friendship grew out of a shared love of music.

oewn-00544490-v.learner: to develop in your feelings, or to become more grown-up.
examples: She really grew as a person during her year abroad.

oewn-00246343-v.learner: to make something grow or develop.
examples: She grew her small shop into a large business.

oewn-00251425-v.learner: to become joined to something by growing, or as if by growing.
examples: The broken bones in his arm grew together in a few weeks.

oewn-02785801-n.learner: a place where ball games are played, especially baseball.
examples: Thousands of fans filled the park for the opening game of the season.

oewn-03896578-n.learner: the position of a car's gears that works as a brake to keep it from moving.
examples: Put the car in park before you get out.

oewn-09910201-n.learner: a person who is being thought of for something, such as a position, a prize, or an honour.
examples: The young player is seen as a strong prospect for the national team.

oewn-00154485-n.learner: a statement of how an illness is likely to develop.
examples: The doctor's prospect for the patient was gloomy: the disease would probably spread.
